title: HO2S Heater Control Circuit High (Bank 1 Sensor 2)
shortDescription: The downstream O2 sensor heater control circuit on bank 1 shows an abnormally high voltage signal.
fullDescription:
P0038 sets when the PCM detects excessive voltage on the heater control circuit of the rear oxygen sensor on bank 1 (after the catalytic converter). The heater helps the sensor reach operating temperature quickly so closed-loop fuel control can start and catalyst efficiency can be monitored.

Common triggers include an open heater element, damaged wiring, a blown fuse, or a failed PCM heater driver. The MIL illuminates and readiness monitors for the catalyst will often remain incomplete.
safetyImpact: No immediate driveability concern, but emissions increase and the vehicle will fail inspection.

causes.cause: Failed heater element inside the O2 sensor
Open or shorted heater circuit wiring

fixSteps.title: Scan and freeze frame
fixSteps.instruction: Record freeze frame data and confirm code is current.

fixSteps.title: Check O2 heater fuse
fixSteps.instruction: Inspect the relevant fuse in the underhood fuse box.

fixSteps.title: Test heater resistance
fixSteps.instruction: Measure heater resistance at the sensor connector; compare to spec (typically 3-15 ohms).

fixSteps.title: Replace sensor if faulty
fixSteps.instruction: Install a new HO2S bank 1 sensor 2 and clear codes.

faq.a: Yes, short-term. However, emissions monitoring will be impaired.

title: Turbo/Super Charger Bypass Valve Control Circuit Range/Performance
shortDescription: The turbocharger bypass valve circuit is operating outside expected parameters.
fullDescription:
P0039 indicates the PCM has detected the turbo or supercharger bypass valve control circuit is not responding within the expected range. The bypass valve vents compressed air during throttle lift to avoid compressor surge.

Causes include a stuck valve, vacuum leaks on the control line, or an electrical fault in the solenoid circuit.
safetyImpact: Possible compressor surge noise and reduced boost response, but not a safety risk.
symptoms: Chuffing or surge noise on lift

fixSteps.title: Inspect bypass valve
fixSteps.instruction: Check valve operation and seal integrity.

fixSteps.title: Check control hoses
fixSteps.instruction: Inspect vacuum hoses to the bypass solenoid for cracks or disconnection.

fixSteps.title: Test solenoid
fixSteps.instruction: Measure resistance and command solenoid with scan tool.

faq.a: Usually no, but repeated surge can trigger overboost codes.

title: O2 Sensor Signals Swapped (Bank 1 Sensor 1 / Bank 2 Sensor 1)
shortDescription: The PCM has detected that the upstream O2 sensor signals between banks appear crossed.
fullDescription:
P0040 sets when the PCM sees the O2 sensor response patterns from bank 1 and bank 2 upstream sensors have been swapped, usually after a repair. The computer recognizes the signal behavior doesn't match the bank it's assigned to.

This is most often caused by installing the sensors on the opposite banks, or by a wiring harness repair error.
safetyImpact: Fuel trims will be incorrectly applied between banks causing rough running.

fixSteps.title: Verify sensor locations
fixSteps.instruction: Confirm bank 1 sensor 1 and bank 2 sensor 1 are installed correctly.

fixSteps.title: Clear and retest
fixSteps.instruction: Clear codes and drive cycle to verify.

faq.q: Can this happen without a recent repair?
faq.a: Very rarely. Usually it appears after sensor replacement.

title: HO2S Heater Control Circuit (Bank 2 Sensor 1)
shortDescription: General fault in the heater control circuit of the upstream O2 sensor on bank 2.
fullDescription:
P0050 sets when the PCM cannot control the heater element on the bank 2 upstream oxygen sensor. This heater is crucial to get the sensor operational quickly at cold start for reduced emissions.

Causes include heater failure, wiring open/short, or blown fuse.
safetyImpact: Delayed closed-loop fuel control, increased cold-start emissions.

causes.cause: Open or short in heater circuit

fixSteps.title: Replace sensor
fixSteps.instruction: Install new HO2S and clear codes.

faq.a: Bank 2 is the side opposite cylinder 1.

title: HO2S Heater Resistance Low (Bank 2 Sensor 1)
shortDescription: Bank 2 upstream O2 sensor heater resistance below specification.
fullDescription:
P0052 indicates the heater resistance on the upstream sensor on bank 2 is lower than expected, suggesting a short inside the heater element or wiring.

The sensor typically needs replacement if the heater element itself has shorted.
safetyImpact: Possible blown fuse and loss of O2 heating function.

fixSteps.title: Inspect harness
fixSteps.instruction: Check for pinched or shorted wiring.

fixSteps.title: Replace sensor
fixSteps.instruction: Install new sensor if heater shorted.

faq.q: Why does my fuse keep blowing?
faq.a: A shorted heater draws excess current and opens the fuse.

title: HO2S Heater Resistance (Bank 1 Sensor 1)
shortDescription: Heater resistance of bank 1 upstream O2 sensor out of range.
fullDescription:
P0053 is set when the PCM measures heater resistance outside acceptable range for the bank 1 upstream oxygen sensor.

The sensor is typically replaced as a unit; connectors and wiring should be inspected first.
safetyImpact: Delayed closed-loop operation and increased cold-start emissions.

faq.a: Yes, upstream means pre-catalyst (front).

title: HO2S Heater Resistance (Bank 1 Sensor 2)
shortDescription: Heater resistance on bank 1 downstream O2 sensor is out of range.
fullDescription:
P0054 indicates abnormal heater element resistance on the post-catalyst O2 sensor (bank 1 sensor 2). The rear sensor is primarily used to monitor catalyst efficiency.

Check wiring first, then replace the sensor if heater is the fault.
safetyImpact: No immediate driveability impact, emissions monitoring affected.

faq.q: Can I use a universal sensor?
faq.a: OE-style direct-fit sensors are more reliable.

title: HO2S Heater Control Circuit (Bank 2 Sensor 2)
shortDescription: Bank 2 downstream O2 sensor heater circuit has a fault.
fullDescription:
P0056 sets when the bank 2 downstream oxygen sensor heater control cannot be properly operated by the PCM. This affects catalyst monitoring on bank 2.

Check fuse, wiring, and heater element.

fixSteps.title: Check fuse
fixSteps.instruction: Inspect O2 heater fuse for bank 2.

fixSteps.title: Replace sensor
fixSteps.instruction: Install new sensor if heater faulty.

faq.a: Yes, with an active heater code.

title: HO2S Heater Control Circuit Low (Bank 2 Sensor 2)
shortDescription: Low voltage detected on the bank 2 downstream O2 heater control circuit.
fullDescription:
P0057 indicates a low voltage condition on the heater control side of the rear bank 2 O2 sensor. This often points to a short-to-ground, open driver, or failed heater element.

Inspect harness first then test heater.
safetyImpact: Catalyst efficiency cannot be properly verified.

causes.cause: Short to ground on control wire

fixSteps.title: Inspect harness
fixSteps.instruction: Look for wear or pinch points.

fixSteps.title: Test circuit
fixSteps.instruction: Measure control-side voltage with key on.

fixSteps.title: Replace sensor
fixSteps.instruction: If heater failed, install new sensor.

faq.a: No, wiring and sensor faults are far more likely.

title: HO2S Heater Control Circuit High (Bank 2 Sensor 2)
shortDescription: Excessive voltage on bank 2 downstream O2 heater circuit.
fullDescription:
P0058 sets when the PCM sees higher-than-expected voltage on the heater control wire of bank 2 sensor 2, typically because the circuit is open.

An open heater element, broken wire, or failed power supply are typical causes.

faq.a: It will return if the heater is actually open.

title: HO2S Heater Resistance (Bank 2 Sensor 2)
shortDescription: Resistance of bank 2 downstream O2 heater is out of range.
fullDescription:
P0060 indicates the heater element resistance on the bank 2 downstream O2 sensor is outside specification. This usually requires sensor replacement after confirming wiring.

Test resistance cold at sensor connector, then compare to spec.

faq.a: Yes, test at room temperature for consistent values.

title: HO2S Heater Control Circuit (Bank 2 Sensor 3)
shortDescription: Heater control fault on the third O2 sensor on bank 2.
fullDescription:
P0062 refers to the third O2 sensor on bank 2 (used on some vehicles with dual catalysts or complex exhaust). The heater control circuit has a general fault.

Inspect wiring, fuse, and heater element.
safetyImpact: Emissions monitoring on affected bank reduced.

fixSteps.title: Replace sensor
fixSteps.instruction: Install new sensor if heater failed.

faq.a: No, only those with additional catalysts or exhaust sections.

title: HO2S Heater Control Circuit Low (Bank 2 Sensor 3)
shortDescription: Low voltage on bank 2 sensor 3 heater control.
fullDescription:
P0063 indicates a short-to-ground or low-voltage condition on the heater control wire of the third bank 2 O2 sensor. This triggers when PCM commands the heater off and sees unexpected low voltage, or when on and voltage stays low.

Fault can be in wiring or heater circuit.
safetyImpact: Loss of sensor data for rear emissions monitor.

faq.a: A post-catalyst sensor on vehicles with multiple cats in series.

title: HO2S Heater Control Circuit High (Bank 2 Sensor 3)
shortDescription: High voltage on bank 2 sensor 3 heater control.
fullDescription:
P0064 indicates an open circuit or unexpectedly high voltage on the heater control of the third bank 2 O2 sensor. Typically traced to an open heater or broken wire.

Measure heater resistance and repair or replace as needed.

faq.a: Only vehicles equipped with three O2 sensors per bank use this DTC.

title: MAP/MAF - Throttle Position Correlation
shortDescription: Manifold pressure/airflow does not match the expected value for the current throttle position.
fullDescription:
P0068 is one of the most common airflow correlation codes. The PCM compares measured MAP or MAF to a calculated value based on throttle position and RPM. A mismatch can indicate vacuum leaks, sensor failure, or throttle body issues.

Large vacuum leaks and dirty MAF sensors are top culprits.
safetyImpact: May cause rough idle, hesitation, or stalling.

faq.q: Can I clean the throttle body myself?
faq.a: Yes, but relearn idle if you do.

title: MAP - Barometric Pressure Correlation
shortDescription: MAP sensor reading at key-on doesn't match barometric pressure.
fullDescription:
P0069 sets when key-on MAP values disagree with the barometric pressure sensor (or expected value). This catches MAP sensor drift or a plugged MAP vacuum line.

A vacuum line issue or failed sensor is typical.

causes.cause: Plugged or leaking MAP vacuum line

fixSteps.title: Test MAP
fixSteps.instruction: Check voltage at key-on vs spec.

faq.a: Yes, baro drops with altitude but the PCM accounts for it.

title: Ambient Air Temperature Sensor Circuit
shortDescription: General circuit fault in the ambient air temp sensor.
fullDescription:
P0070 sets when the PCM sees an unreliable signal from the ambient air temperature sensor. This sensor influences fuel enrichment, A/C operation, and gauge display.

Wiring and sensor replacement typically resolve the issue.
safetyImpact: No driveability concern; may affect A/C automatic modes.

faq.a: Sensor at the front bumper reads incorrectly when faulty.

title: Ambient Air Temp Sensor Range/Performance
shortDescription: Ambient temp sensor reading is not changing as expected.
fullDescription:
P0071 indicates the ambient temp reading is either stuck or changes too slowly vs. other temperature inputs (IAT, ECT at cold start). Often a stuck sensor.

Replace the sensor if verified faulty.
safetyImpact: Minor effect on climate control logic.

fixSteps.title: Compare readings
fixSteps.instruction: Compare IAT, ECT, ambient at cold start.

faq.a: No, but ice-warning logic relies on this sensor.

title: Ambient Air Temp Sensor Low Input
shortDescription: Ambient sensor signal voltage is low (shorted to ground).
fullDescription:
P0072 indicates an implausibly low voltage from the ambient temp sensor, typically meaning a short to ground or a failed sensor.

Check wiring and connector first.

faq.a: Short to ground reads as extreme temperature.

title: Ambient Air Temp Sensor High Input
shortDescription: Ambient sensor signal voltage is high (open circuit).
fullDescription:
P0073 indicates high signal voltage from the ambient temp sensor, typically an open circuit at the sensor or wiring.

Measure voltage at sensor connector and inspect harness.

faq.a: Open circuit defaults to the lowest sensor range value.

title: Ambient Air Temp Sensor Intermittent
shortDescription: Ambient temp sensor signal is intermittent.
fullDescription:
P0074 sets when the ambient sensor reading intermittently drops out. Usually a connector or wiring issue. Wiggle-testing the harness often reproduces the fault.

Clean/reseat connector or replace sensor.

faq.a: Loose or corroded connector pins cause dropouts.

title: Intake Valve Control Solenoid Circuit (Bank 1)
shortDescription: General fault in the bank 1 variable intake valve control solenoid circuit.
fullDescription:
P0075 indicates the PCM detects a circuit fault with the bank 1 intake valve control solenoid (VVT/variable intake system).

Check wiring and solenoid resistance; replace as needed.

faq.q: Is this the same as VVT?
faq.a: Yes, on many platforms the intake valve control is VVT.

title: Intake Valve Control Solenoid Circuit Low (Bank 1)
shortDescription: Low voltage on the bank 1 intake valve control solenoid circuit.
fullDescription:
P0076 sets when PCM sees low voltage on the control side of the intake valve solenoid, often a shorted wire or stuck solenoid.

Inspect harness then bench-test solenoid.

faq.a: Clean oil is important because VVT solenoids are sensitive to debris.

title: Intake Valve Control Solenoid Circuit High (Bank 1)
shortDescription: High voltage on the bank 1 intake valve control solenoid circuit.
fullDescription:
P0077 indicates PCM sees high voltage on the solenoid control line (open circuit). Common with broken wire or failed solenoid coil.

Repair harness or replace solenoid.

faq.a: Yes, but with reduced performance.

title: Exhaust Valve Control Solenoid Circuit (Bank 1)
shortDescription: General fault in the bank 1 exhaust VVT solenoid circuit.
fullDescription:
P0078 indicates the PCM has detected a general electrical fault on the bank 1 exhaust valve control solenoid. Like its intake counterpart, this solenoid alters exhaust cam timing.

Fault-finding mirrors the intake VVT solenoid.

faq.a: Short term yes, but fix promptly to avoid related VVT damage.

title: Exhaust Valve Control Solenoid Circuit Low (Bank 1)
shortDescription: Low voltage on bank 1 exhaust VVT solenoid.
fullDescription:
P0079 is set when low voltage is detected on the bank 1 exhaust VVT solenoid control line, often due to a short to ground or failed coil.

Wiring and solenoid checks as usual.

faq.a: Yes, VVT components need clean oil to function.

title: Exhaust Valve Control Solenoid Circuit High (Bank 1)
shortDescription: High voltage on bank 1 exhaust VVT solenoid.
fullDescription:
P0080 indicates an open circuit or high-voltage condition on the bank 1 exhaust VVT solenoid control line. Typical causes include a broken wire or failed coil.

Replace the solenoid or repair harness.

faq.a: Usually no; they're replaced as a unit.

title: Purge Flow Sensor Circuit Low
shortDescription: EVAP purge flow sensor signal is too low.
fullDescription:
P0468 sets when the EVAP purge flow sensor reports unexpectedly low flow, or a low-voltage signal indicating a sensor or circuit issue.

Check sensor and wiring; also inspect purge valve.

faq.a: No, but repair before next inspection.

title: Purge Flow Sensor Circuit Intermittent
shortDescription: Purge flow sensor signal drops out intermittently.
fullDescription:
P0469 indicates intermittent signal from the EVAP purge flow sensor. Usually wiring or connector related.

Inspect harness and connector.

faq.a: Yes, applied to a clean connector.

title: Exhaust Pressure Sensor Range/Performance
shortDescription: Exhaust pressure sensor signal out of expected range.
fullDescription:
P0471 indicates the exhaust backpressure sensor signal does not match expected values based on engine operating conditions. Common on diesel and turbo vehicles.

Check sensor tube for clogging and sensor itself.
safetyImpact: Possible reduced power and emissions increase.

faq.a: Yes, carbon buildup plugs the pressure tube.

title: Exhaust Pressure Sensor Low
shortDescription: Exhaust pressure sensor signal is too low.
fullDescription:
P0472 indicates a low signal from the exhaust backpressure sensor, usually from a plugged tube or failed sensor.

Clean the pressure tube and retest.

faq.a: Carbon buildup from diesel soot or EGR residue.

title: Exhaust Pressure Sensor High
shortDescription: Exhaust pressure sensor signal too high.
fullDescription:
P0473 indicates the sensor reports very high voltage or pressure, sometimes due to a failed sensor or excessive actual exhaust restriction (e.g., clogged DPF).

Always verify real pressure before replacing sensor.
safetyImpact: A plugged DPF can cause power loss.

fixSteps.title: Regen or replace
fixSteps.instruction: Force DPF regen or replace sensor.

faq.a: Force regen first, then replace if needed.

title: Exhaust Pressure Sensor Intermittent
shortDescription: Intermittent signal from the exhaust pressure sensor.
fullDescription:
P0474 sets with an intermittent signal fault, often due to loose wiring or partial blockage in the pressure line.

Inspect harness and clean the pressure tube.

faq.a: Yes, but it typically returns if not fixed.

title: Exhaust Pressure Control Valve Malfunction
shortDescription: Exhaust backpressure control valve operating incorrectly.
fullDescription:
P0475 indicates the exhaust backpressure control valve (used for DPF regen or cold-start heat retention) is not operating correctly. Common on diesel trucks.

Check actuator and wiring.

faq.a: Yes, affects DPF regen strategy.

title: Exhaust Pressure Control Valve Range/Performance
shortDescription: Exhaust backpressure control valve response out of range.
fullDescription:
P0476 indicates the exhaust backpressure control valve response does not match commanded position within the expected time or range.

Inspect for carbon buildup and actuator fault.

faq.a: No, that's illegal on road-going vehicles.

title: Exhaust Pressure Control Valve Low
shortDescription: Low voltage signal from exhaust backpressure control valve.
fullDescription:
P0477 means a low-voltage condition on the backpressure valve control circuit, typically due to a short to ground or failed coil.

Inspect wiring and replace actuator if confirmed bad.

faq.a: Long-term DPF issues may develop.

title: Exhaust Pressure Control Valve High
shortDescription: High voltage signal from exhaust backpressure control valve.
fullDescription:
P0478 indicates high voltage (open circuit) on the backpressure valve control line. Common causes are a broken wire or failed actuator coil.

Inspect harness and replace actuator if needed.

faq.a: Mostly on diesel trucks with EBPR systems.

title: Exhaust Pressure Control Valve Intermittent
shortDescription: Intermittent operation of exhaust backpressure control valve.
fullDescription:
P0479 indicates intermittent faults with the exhaust backpressure control valve, typically wiring or corroded connector.

Inspect harness and connector.

faq.a: Usually a marginal connector.

title: EGR Control Circuit A Low
shortDescription: Low voltage on EGR A control circuit.
fullDescription:
P0489 sets when the PCM detects low voltage on the EGR valve control circuit A, usually a short to ground or failed actuator coil.

Test wiring and actuator.
safetyImpact: Increased NOx emissions and possible knock.

faq.a: EGR off can increase in-cylinder temps and cause knock.

title: EGR Control Circuit A High
shortDescription: High voltage on EGR A control circuit.
fullDescription:
P0490 sets when high voltage (open circuit) is detected on EGR control circuit A. Commonly due to a broken wire or open coil.

Test the valve coil and inspect harness.

fixSteps.title: Replace valve
fixSteps.instruction: Install new EGR valve if needed.

faq.a: Fairly common on carbon-fouled EGR valves.

title: Secondary Air Injection System Insufficient Flow (Bank 1)
shortDescription: Not enough flow from the secondary air injection system on bank 1.
fullDescription:
P0491 indicates the PCM expected more airflow from the secondary air injection system on bank 1 during cold-start emissions reduction. Causes include plugged passages, a failed pump, or stuck check valves.

Typically sets only briefly after cold start during the monitor.

faq.a: No, many newer cars don't.

title: Secondary Air Injection System Insufficient Flow (Bank 2)
shortDescription: Not enough flow from secondary air injection system on bank 2.
fullDescription:
P0492 is the bank 2 counterpart to P0491. Secondary air injection on bank 2 is insufficient during cold-start monitoring.

Check pump, hoses, and check valves on bank 2.

faq.a: Each bank has its own check valve and supply.

title: EGT Sensor Circuit High (Bank 1 Sensor 1)
shortDescription: Exhaust gas temp sensor signal too high on bank 1 sensor 1.
fullDescription:
P0543 sets when the EGT sensor on bank 1 sensor 1 reads implausibly high or is open circuit. Used on diesels and some gasoline turbo applications.

Check wiring and sensor resistance.

faq.a: Yes, DPF regen logic depends on EGT.

title: EGT Sensor Circuit (Bank 1 Sensor 1)
shortDescription: General circuit fault with bank 1 sensor 1 EGT sensor.
fullDescription:
P0544 is a general circuit-fault code for the EGT sensor at bank 1 sensor 1 location. Affects DPF regeneration and turbo protection logic.

Inspect wiring and test sensor.

faq.a: Usually not; sensors are replaced.

title: EGT Sensor Circuit Low (Bank 1 Sensor 1)
shortDescription: Low voltage on EGT sensor bank 1 sensor 1.
fullDescription:
P0545 indicates low voltage (short to ground) from the bank 1 EGT sensor. Caused by a shorted sensor or harness.

Test and repair accordingly.

faq.a: May be disabled until fixed.

title: EGT Sensor Circuit High (Bank 1 Sensor 2)
shortDescription: High voltage on bank 1 sensor 2 EGT circuit.
fullDescription:
P0546 sets when bank 1 sensor 2 EGT reads high voltage or open circuit. Typical on diesel vehicles with multiple EGT sensors for DPF management.

Replace sensor or repair wiring.

faq.a: Yes, diesels often have 3-4 along the exhaust.

title: EGT Sensor Circuit (Bank 2 Sensor 1)
shortDescription: General circuit fault on bank 2 sensor 1 EGT sensor.
fullDescription:
P0547 indicates an EGT circuit fault on bank 2 sensor 1. The PCM relies on this to manage turbo and DPF thermal protection.

Inspect wiring and sensor.

faq.a: Mostly, but some gas turbos also use EGT sensors.

title: EGT Sensor Circuit Low (Bank 2 Sensor 1)
shortDescription: Low voltage on bank 2 sensor 1 EGT circuit.
fullDescription:
P0548 means bank 2 sensor 1 EGT reads low voltage (short to ground). Typically due to shorted wiring or failed sensor.

Test wiring and sensor.

faq.a: Side opposite cylinder 1.

title: EGT Sensor Circuit High (Bank 2 Sensor 1)
shortDescription: High voltage on bank 2 sensor 1 EGT circuit.
fullDescription:
P0549 indicates high voltage (open) on bank 2 sensor 1 EGT sensor circuit. Usually broken wiring or failed sensor.

Replace as needed.

faq.q: Do I need an OE sensor?
faq.a: OE recommended for accuracy.

title: Power Steering Pressure Sensor Circuit
shortDescription: General circuit fault with the power steering pressure sensor.
fullDescription:
P0550 sets when the PCM detects an abnormal signal from the power steering pressure sensor. The sensor helps the PCM boost idle RPM during parking maneuvers.

Check wiring and sensor.
safetyImpact: Possible low idle when turning wheel.

faq.a: Yes, but idle may dip at parking speed.

title: Power Steering Pressure Sensor Range/Performance (Alt Definition)
shortDescription: PS pressure sensor reading is out of range during driving.
fullDescription:
P0551-v2 represents a range/performance issue where the power steering pressure sensor reads within electrical range but doesn't change with driving conditions. This alternative description matches vehicles that differentiate this fault from a hard circuit fault.

Check sensor function by observing with scan tool while turning the wheel stopped vs driving.
safetyImpact: Idle response at low speed affected.

faq.a: Yes, check level first.

title: Power Steering Pressure Sensor Low Input (Alt Definition)
shortDescription: Low voltage from PS pressure sensor.
fullDescription:
P0552-v2 indicates a low-voltage signal from the power steering pressure sensor. Common with a short to ground or failed sensor.

Test circuit and replace as necessary.

faq.a: No, only PCM idle compensation.

title: Power Steering Pressure Sensor Intermittent
shortDescription: Intermittent signal from PS pressure sensor.
fullDescription:
P0554 sets when the PS pressure sensor signal drops intermittently. Usually wiring or connector related.

Inspect and repair harness.

faq.a: Yes short term, but fix before inspection.

title: Generator Control Circuit Malfunction (Alt Definition)
shortDescription: Fault in the alternator control circuit.
fullDescription:
P0620-v3 is an alternative description for a generator control circuit fault. The PCM monitors the charging circuit and detects a malfunction in the control line to the alternator.

Check alternator wiring and perform charging system test.
safetyImpact: Battery may discharge and car stall.

faq.a: Fix promptly to avoid stalling.

title: Fuel Pump A Control Circuit Low
shortDescription: Low voltage on fuel pump control circuit.
fullDescription:
P0628 indicates the PCM sees low voltage (short to ground) on the fuel pump control circuit, which may prevent fuel pump operation.

Test the pump relay, wiring, and PCM driver.

causes.cause: Short to ground on control wire

faq.a: PCM disables pump when circuit is shorted.

title: Fuel Pump A Control Circuit High
shortDescription: High voltage on fuel pump control circuit.
fullDescription:
P0629 indicates high voltage (open circuit) on the fuel pump control line. This can mean a broken wire, open relay, or PCM driver issue.

Test relay and wiring first.

faq.a: Only after all wiring and relay tests pass.

title: Odometer Not Programmed In PCM
shortDescription: PCM odometer value not programmed.
fullDescription:
P0632 indicates the PCM's stored odometer value is not programmed or mismatches the cluster. Often appears after PCM replacement without programming.

Requires dealer or capable scan tool to program.

fixSteps.title: Program PCM
fixSteps.instruction: Use manufacturer scan tool to program odometer.

faq.a: Only with bidirectional scan tool; otherwise a shop.

title: Sensor Reference Voltage A Circuit High
shortDescription: Reference voltage output from PCM is too high.
fullDescription:
P0643 sets when the PCM's 5V sensor reference circuit A is showing higher-than-expected voltage. Many sensors can be affected.

Inspect for shorts to higher voltage sources.
safetyImpact: Multiple sensor readings incorrect; may cause driveability issues.

fixSteps.title: Disconnect sensors
fixSteps.instruction: Disconnect sensors one at a time and monitor voltage.

faq.a: Reference circuit powers many sensors.

title: Actuator Supply Voltage A Circuit/Open
shortDescription: Actuator supply voltage circuit open or not supplying power.
fullDescription:
P0657 indicates the PCM-controlled actuator supply voltage line is open. Many actuators may fail to function as a result.

Check relevant relay, fuse, and PCM internal driver.

faq.a: The dedicated PCM output powering multiple actuators.

title: Actuator Supply Voltage A Circuit Low
shortDescription: Low voltage on actuator supply circuit.
fullDescription:
P0658 sets when the actuator supply voltage circuit A is lower than expected (short to ground). This disables many actuators.

Check wiring for shorts.

faq.a: Only if wiring checks pass.

title: Actuator Supply Voltage A Circuit High
shortDescription: High voltage on actuator supply circuit.
fullDescription:
P0659 indicates the actuator supply voltage circuit A is higher than expected. Short to battery voltage is most common.

Inspect wiring and PCM connector.

fixSteps.title: Test wiring
fixSteps.instruction: Check for short to battery voltage.

faq.a: Yes, extended overvoltage can cause failures.

title: Intake Manifold Tuning Valve Control Circuit/Open (Bank 1)
shortDescription: Open circuit on bank 1 intake manifold tuning valve control.
fullDescription:
P0660 indicates the PCM has detected an open circuit on the bank 1 intake manifold runner control (tuning) valve. The tuning valve alters runner length/air path for torque and power optimization.

Inspect wiring and solenoid.

faq.a: Yes, but torque curve changes.

title: Intake Manifold Tuning Valve Control Circuit Low (Bank 1)
shortDescription: Low voltage on bank 1 intake manifold tuning valve circuit.
fullDescription:
P0661 indicates a low-voltage condition (short to ground) on the bank 1 intake manifold tuning valve control. Wiring or solenoid fault is typical.

Inspect harness and replace solenoid if bad.

faq.a: Slightly, as intake tuning also affects efficiency.

title: Intake Manifold Tuning Valve Control Circuit High (Bank 1)
shortDescription: High voltage on bank 1 intake manifold tuning valve circuit.
fullDescription:
P0662 indicates high-voltage (open) condition on the bank 1 intake manifold tuning valve control. Broken wire or failed coil are typical.

Test and replace as needed.

faq.a: Varies; many are electric solenoids driving vacuum actuators.

title: Intake Manifold Tuning Valve Control Circuit/Open (Bank 2)
shortDescription: Open circuit on bank 2 intake manifold tuning valve control.
fullDescription:
P0663 is the bank 2 counterpart to P0660. The PCM detects an open circuit on the bank 2 tuning valve control line.

Inspect and repair harness or replace solenoid.

faq.a: Yes, bank 2 codes apply to V and horizontally opposed engines.

title: Intake Manifold Tuning Valve Control Circuit Low (Bank 2)
shortDescription: Low voltage on bank 2 intake manifold tuning valve circuit.
fullDescription:
P0664 indicates a short-to-ground or low-voltage condition on the bank 2 intake manifold tuning valve control. Check wiring and solenoid.

Replace solenoid if damaged.

faq.a: Typically no, but torque may be noticeably lower.
